records.title: Climate, Justice, and Energy Solutions
records.header: ATMOS 100 Climate, Justice, and Energy Solutions (5) SSc/NSc, DIV
records.text: ATMOS 100 Climate, Justice, and Energy Solutions (5) SSc/NSc, DIV Presents visions of the future when the climate crisis is solved. Describes paths towards reaching these goals. Solutions include building a resilient society with clean energy, sustainable agriculture, climate justice, and a just transition for workers.

records.title: Understanding and Predicting the Weather
records.header: ATMOS 101 Understanding and Predicting the Weather (5) NSc
records.text: ATMOS 101 Understanding and Predicting the Weather (5) NSc Students learn the essentials about weather, including basic concepts on how to read the sky, and how to interpret weather information and forecasts from a variety of sources. Covers origin and structure of the atmosphere, wind, rain, and snow storms, and other major weather features, as well as how weather forecasts are made and evaluated. Offered: AWSpS.

records.title: Hurricanes and Thunderstorms: Their Science and Impact
records.header: ATMOS 103 Hurricanes and Thunderstorms: Their Science and Impact (3) NSc/SSc
records.text: ATMOS 103 Hurricanes and Thunderstorms: Their Science and Impact (3) NSc/SSc Explores the science, history, and impacts of thunderstorms and hurricanes. Includes basic processes responsible for thunderstorms and hurricanes and for the lightning, hail, high winds, and storm surges that accompany them. Presents significant historical examples, along with the impact on human activities, strategies for personal safety, and societal adaptation. Offered: SpS.

records.title: Global Warming: Understanding the Issues
records.header: ATMOS 111 Global Warming: Understanding the Issues (5) SSc/NSc
records.text: ATMOS 111 Global Warming: Understanding the Issues (5) SSc/NSc Presents a broad overview of the science of global warming. Includes the causes, evidence, and societal and environmental impacts from the last century. Recounts future climate projections and societal decisions that influence greenhouse gas emission scenarios and our ability to adapt to climate change. Presents ways to identify disinformation versus correct science. Offered: AWSpS.

records.title: Climate and Climate Change
records.header: ATMOS 211 Climate and Climate Change (5) NSc/SSc
records.text: ATMOS 211 Climate and Climate Change (5) NSc/SSc Explores the nature, stability, and sensitivity of the global climate system. Examines factors influencing climate, including interactions among the atmosphere, oceans, solid earth, and biosphere. Investigates global warming, ozone depletion, and other human influences. Intended for non-majors. Course overlaps with: ESS 201. Offered: AWSp.

records.title: Air Pollution: Societal Impacts and Solutions
records.header: ATMOS 212 Air Pollution: Societal Impacts and Solutions (3) SSc/NSc
records.text: ATMOS 212 Air Pollution: Societal Impacts and Solutions (3) SSc/NSc Explores the causes, impacts, and solutions for air pollution on local, regional, and global scales. Topics include urban smog, wildfires, acid rain, the ozone hole, and contrasts between indoor and outdoor air pollution. Health and environmental effects of air pollutants, technological solutions, environmental justice, and international policy regulations. Offered: AWSp.

records.text: ATMOS 220 Exploring Atmospheric and Climate Science (1, max. 2) NSc Focuses on current research in atmospheric and climate science and the related implications for public health, business, and environmental policy. Credit/no-credit only.

records.title: Introduction to Atmospheric Sciences
records.header: ATMOS 301 Introduction to Atmospheric Sciences (5) NSc
records.text: ATMOS 301 Introduction to Atmospheric Sciences (5) NSc Composition and structure of the atmosphere. Clouds and weather phenomena. Thermodynamic processes. Solar and terrestrial radiation. Air motions. Daily weather discussions and forecasts. For majors and nonmajors. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in MATH 124; a minimum grade of 2.0 in MATH 125; a minimum grade of 2.0 in MATH 126; a minimum grade of 2.0 in PHYS 121; a minimum grade of 2.0 in PHYS 122; and a minimum grade of 2.0 in PHYS 123. Offered: A.

records.title: The Science of Climate
records.header: ATMOS 321 The Science of Climate (3) NSc
records.text: ATMOS 321 The Science of Climate (3) NSc Evolution and present state of earth's climate. Emphasis on physical processes determining the climate of the earth's atmosphere and surface: radiative transfer, energy balance, hydrologic cycle, and atmospheric and oceanic energy transport. Factors controlling climate change. Prerequisite: a minimum grade of 2.0 in MATH 124; a minimum grade of 2.0 in MATH 125; a minimum grade of 2.0 in MATH 126; a minimum grade of 2.0 in PHYS 121; a minimum grade of 2.0 in PHYS 122; and a minimum grade of 2.0 in PHYS 123. Offered: Sp.

Prerequisite: ATMOS 101 or ATMOS 301.
